claims.text: Retention of a single-phase solid solution at high operating temperatures is governed by the balance between mixing entropy and relief of localized lattice strain.
Atomic-size mismatch and short-range ordering produce localized lattice distortions.
Nanoparticles maintain structural and chemical stability from 473 K to 1923 K when lattice distortions remain below a critical threshold.
The initial nanoparticles are defect-minimized, compositionally uniform solid solutions containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
Selecting constituent metals with smaller atomic-size differences reduces lattice strain relative to selecting metals with larger atomic-size differences.
Localized lattice distortion and short-range atomic ordering mediate strain relief and structural stability.
High mixing entropy favors a homogeneous distribution of metals.
Excessive atomic-size disparity creates localized lattice strain whose energy can overcome entropic stabilization at high temperature.
Overcoming entropic stabilization through excessive lattice strain drives phase separation and elemental segregation.
Nanoparticles with minimized lattice strain will retain a single-phase solid solution during thermal cycling from 473 K to 1923 K in an inert atmosphere.
Nanoparticles with minimized lattice strain will retain stable catalytic and thermoelectric performance during thermal cycling.
Nanoparticles with larger atomic-size mismatches will form secondary phases or exhibit elemental segregation during thermal cycling.
Phase separation or elemental segregation in the high-mismatch nanoparticles will be accompanied by catalytic or thermoelectric performance degradation.
The initial solid solution has homogeneous elemental distribution and stable performance at ambient temperature.
Oxidative conditions or processing impurities may independently alter nanoparticle stability.
The critical lattice-distortion threshold for phase separation varies with metal combination and particle size.
